prompt: We have a few million mostly idle topics and want the broker to release their memory without losing any data, so we turned on brokerCloseInactiveTopicsEnabled. The broker refuses to start if brokerDeleteInactiveTopicsEnabled is also true, and also if brokerDeleteInactiveTopicsMode is delete_when_subscriptions_caught_up. Why those two restrictions? And what happens to a namespace whose inactive-topic policy sets deleteWhileInactive=true while this is on?
key: PIP-470 (pip/pip-470.md, "Close Inactive Topics Without Deleting Them", added 2026-08-27). Close mode reuses the delete-GC inactivity detection but unloads the topic instead of deleting it: only the in-memory topic is released, and BookKeeper ledgers, metadata, subscriptions, cursors and topic policies stay, so the next client reloads it. The two flags pick the action GC takes, so they are mutually exclusive and only one may be on (PulsarService fails fast at start). Close mode supports only delete_when_no_subscriptions because under delete_when_subscriptions_caught_up a topic counts as inactive as soon as its subscriptions are caught up, even while consumers are connected; closing it would disconnect them, they would reconnect and reload it, and GC would close it again — an unload/reload loop that frees no memory. Under delete_when_no_subscriptions any subscription keeps the topic active, so a topic is closed only once every client has gone. If a namespace or topic policy overrides the mode at runtime, checkGC skips the close for that topic. While close mode is on it takes precedence over a namespace- or topic-level deleteWhileInactive: those topics are closed, never deleted, so data is preserved broker-wide. The retention check is skipped for the close branch since nothing is deleted. Code: PersistentTopic.checkGC and NonPersistentTopic.checkGC, AbstractTopic.isCloseWhileInactive, the validation in PulsarService.

sources.quote: Mutual exclusion with `brokerDeleteInactiveTopicsEnabled`: only one of the two may be enabled at a time.
Under `delete_when_subscriptions_caught_up`, `isActive()` only checks `hasBacklogs()` — a topic whose subscriptions are all caught up is "inactive" **even while consumers are connected**.
The result is a permanent unload/reload loop that frees no memory
Inactive topics are closed, never deleted, so the data-preservation guarantee holds broker-wide rather than only for namespaces that happen to leave the policy unset.
BookKeeper ledgers, topic metadata, subscriptions, cursors, and topic-level policies are all retained.
a namespace- or topic-level policy that overrides the mode at runtime disables close for that topic rather than closing it.
